← Incident Postmortem Timeline

How to write a blameless postmortem from a timeline

The hard part of a postmortem is rarely the analysis. It is rebuilding what happened, in order, from a chat scroll and three dashboards while memory is still fresh. Do that first, and the discussion can be about the system instead of who remembers what.

The four numbers

  • Time to detect — start of impact to the first alert or customer report. A large number here points at monitoring, not at responders.
  • Time to acknowledge — detection to a person taking ownership. Points at paging and on-call routing.
  • Time to mitigate — start to the first rollback, failover or workaround that reduced impact. Usually the number users feel.
  • Time to resolve — start to the all-clear. Averaged over many incidents this is MTTR.

Steps

  1. Copy timestamped lines from chat, the pager and your deploy log into one list. Include the boring ones: who joined, what was checked.
  2. Tag the lines that define the phases (start:, detected:, acknowledged:, mitigated:, resolved:) if wording alone is ambiguous.
  3. Look at the silent gaps first. Thirty minutes with nothing logged usually hides a question: what was being tried, or what was nobody able to see?
  4. Write impact in terms of users and time, not blame. Name roles and systems rather than individuals.
  5. Ask why until you reach a missing guard, alert or runbook step. Each becomes an action item with one owner and a date.
  6. For repeated incidents, add node postmortem.mjs incident.txt --max-ttr 60m to a script to track resolution against a target.

What this does not tell you

It measures only what was written down, and it guesses phases from wording. The draft leaves root cause, impact and action items to your team. It is a starting point and not professional advice.

No warranty. Provided free and as-is. Best-effort hosting, no SLA. The page makes no network calls and uploads nothing. Build a timeline.

INCIDENT POSTMORTEM TIMELINE · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

Paste the incident log. Get the postmortem draft.

Incident platforms such as incident.io, FireHydrant and Rootly build timelines inside a paid product. This page does the core of it for free: paste timestamped lines from chat, a pager or your terminal and get time to detect, acknowledge, mitigate and resolve, the longest stretches where nothing was logged, and a blameless postmortem in Markdown.

Nothing is uploaded. The log you paste is read in this browser and never leaves your device, and this tool makes no network calls of its own. Phases are guessed from wording; tag any line with start:, detected:, ack:, mitigated: or resolved: to be exact.

Paste your timeline

Paste lines that each start with a time, then click Build timeline.

Response metrics

Time (UTC)PhaseEvent

Silent gaps

    Postmortem draft (Markdown)

    Want it in a script?

    Same logic, zero dependencies. It reads one local file (or stdin) and nothing else:

    node postmortem.mjs incident.txt                       # metrics
node postmortem.mjs incident.txt --md --title "Checkout outage" > postmortem.md
node postmortem.mjs incident.txt --max-ttr 60m         # exit 1 if resolve took longer

    Get postmortem.mjs and classify.mjs from the repo. Node 18+, nothing to install, no network calls.

    Common questions

    How do I calculate MTTR from an incident log?

    Mark when impact started and when service was restored, then subtract. This tool does it for each phase: time to detect is start to the first alert or report, time to acknowledge is detection to a human picking it up, time to mitigate is start to the first rollback or workaround, and time to resolve is start to the all-clear. MTTR across many incidents is the average of the resolve times.

    How does it know which line is which phase?

    It looks for plain wording such as alert fired, acknowledged, rolled back and incident closed. If a line is misread, begin it with a tag: start:, detected:, ack:, mitigated: or resolved:. A tag always wins over guessing.

    What timestamp formats work?

    Each line starts with a time such as 14:09, 14:09:30 or 2026-10-03 14:09, optionally followed by Z or an offset like +02:00. Lines with only a time use the date of the last dated line, and a time that goes backwards is read as the next day.

    Does this tool upload my incident log?

    No. The log is read in this page and never leaves your device. The page makes no network calls, and the CLI reads one local file.

    Is the postmortem draft finished?

    No. It fills in the timeline and metrics and leaves impact, root cause and action items for your team to write. It is a starting point and not professional advice.
